# HWaterfallChart

> Cumulative increases, decreases and subtotal resets drawn as offset HTML bars.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HWaterfallChart` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-waterfall-chart>`.
- Constructor: `HearthWaterfallChartElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HWaterfallChart.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Delta items move the running total; kind=total draws from zero and resets it. initial defaults to zero. Native HTML bars encode positive/negative changes with named keyboard controls and a running-total table. The first maxPoints items are shown (default 60, maximum 240). Invalid numbers become zero. Narrow containers scroll within the chart.

## Public API

items: WaterfallItem[] · label, selected, unit: string · initial, height, maxPoints: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    items: WaterfallItem[];
    label: string;
    initial?: number;
    unit?: string;
    selected?: string;
    height?: number;
    maxPoints?: number;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ items: () => [], initial: 0, unit: "", height: 180, maxPoints: 60 }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, column, bar

Use `hearth-waterfall-chart::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface WaterfallItem extends ChartPoint {
    kind?: "delta" | "total";
}

export interface ChartPoint {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    value: number;
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HWaterfallChart } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HWaterfallChart label="Monthly cost" unit="USD" :items="[{id:'base',label:'Base',value:100,kind:'total'},{id:'compute',label:'Compute',value:45},{id:'credit',label:'Credit',value:-20},{id:'total',label:'Total',value:125,kind:'total'}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-waterfall-chart');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Monthly cost",
  "unit": "USD",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "base",
      "label": "Base",
      "value": 100,
      "kind": "total"
    },
    {
      "id": "compute",
      "label": "Compute",
      "value": 45
    },
    {
      "id": "credit",
      "label": "Credit",
      "value": -20
    },
    {
      "id": "total",
      "label": "Total",
      "value": 125,
      "kind": "total"
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```

- [HBarChart](../bar-chart/llms.txt): Native HTML bars with focusable values, selection, and a readable data table.
